name: Locus coeruleus noradrenergic (A6) neuron
anatomy_mentioned: lateral floor/margin of the fourth ventricle
periventricular grey matter of the rostral hindbrain
morphology_summary: Medium-to-large multipolar neuron with a plump soma (~35-45 um) and relatively short dendrites; somata densely packed in a compact core (~1500 neurons/side in mouse, ~25% with a neighbour within 25 um) while dendrites extend into the peri-LC surround. Caudal LC/subcoeruleus additionally contains smaller (~15 um) fusiform cells with triangular somata and two long dendritic tufts. Axons arborise across nearly the whole neuraxis (cortex, hippocampus, amygdala, thalamus, hypothalamus, cerebellum, brainstem, spinal cord).
ephys_summary: Slow spontaneous pacemaker firing ~1-2 Hz in slice (~1-5 Hz across preparations) with broad action potentials and subthreshold oscillation; standard slice ID uses tonic spontaneous firing plus absence of Ih and little/no hyperpolarising sag. Switches from tonic to phasic burst discharge to salient stimuli. Strong alpha2 autoreceptor-mediated self-inhibition (stronger in hippocampus-projecting than mPFC-projecting cells). Dendritic gap-junction electrical coupling between nearby same-type neurons. Compartment-specific glutamatergic drive (GluA1/VGLUT2 somatic, GluA1-GluA4/VGLUT1 distal dendritic); intrinsic CO2/H+ sensitivity.
subtypes_noted: Report treats the LC-NE population as one classical type that is internally heterogeneous rather than as discrete named subtypes: (i) at least two major morpho-electric types with coupling preferentially within type (McKinney et al., 2023); (ii) projection-defined subgroups (mPFC-, hippocampus-, cerebellum-projecting) differing in alpha2 autoreceptor inhibition (Wagner-Altendorf et al., 2019) and cortical-module-specific signals (Breton-Provencher et al., 2022); (iii) graded dorsal-vs-ventral molecular/positional gradients tied to projection bias and task coding (Su et al., 2026); (iv) developmental partition: >99% En1-derived, r0-derived dorsal vs r1-derived ventral components, mostly Pax7+ alar-plate origin with a smaller Pax7-negative subpopulation having sparse thalamic projections (Plummer et al., 2017; Chandler et al., 2019); (v) four genetically separable mature NE subpopulations across the rostral hindbrain, some projecting to cortex from outside LC proper (Robertson et al., 2013); (vi) Phox2a+/TH-negative 'resting noradrenergic' cells in rostral LC (Terrier et al., 2024); (vii) continuum with subcoeruleus/A7 and the wider A4/A5/A7 LC complex (Manger et al., 2021).

name: Peri-locus coeruleus GABAergic neuron
anatomy_mentioned: heterogeneous surround of the locus coeruleus core
morphology_summary: Non-noradrenergic (TH-negative) cells intermingled in the heterogeneous surround of the densely packed LC core; juxtacellular recording found morphologies broadly similar to TH-positive LC neurons.
ephys_summary: TH-negative peri-LC cells respond to foot shock with excitation but show weaker foot-shock responses and less post-activation firing suppression than TH-positive neurons, plus different spontaneous firing rates, spike waveforms and temporal spiking properties.
subtypes_noted: Only weakly resolved in this report: single-cell plus spatial transcriptomics identifies several distinct peri-LC neuronal cell types underlying peri-LC functional diversity (Luskin et al., 2025). Supporting evidence is thin (4 sources); proposed as a contrast/boundary population rather than a subject of the report.
